items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: "Or, 'Jack Teagarden I wrote this for.' One time I had to imitate a dog eating dog food [scats]."

ctx.x: And he played trombone, and later became one of the big Hollywood writers and composers, and I guess everybody knows his song “Harlem Nocturne” it became like a real standard. And so my brother got interested in the trombone from Earle, and he bought his old trombone from him. I think it was two dollars or something like that, a beat up old horn. And that horn went down to my brother Jack — well first of all, after a year in Hollywood we went back to Mobile and took that trombone with us. Let’s see. When my…
Yeah, I know, we’ll get to that. So you had a basically a high school education as far as your trombone and then —
